institutionalPilot.title: Tell us about your institution
institutionalPilot.subtitle: We work directly with a small number of institutions each quarter. Before we schedule a technical call, help us understand where you stand — what's slowing down your treasury, compliance team, or settlement infrastructure.
institutionalPilot.placeholder:
For example: "Our cross-border settlement runs on T+2 SWIFT rails. Counterparty exposure during that window cost us $3M last year alone. We're evaluating whether DLT-native atomic settlement could replace — or run alongside — our current infrastructure, and whether it can pass MiCA compliance requirements without custom middleware."

Describe your current challenge, the metric that matters most to your CFO, and the timeline you're working against.

modal.title: How
modal.subtitle: The organisation has moved from a corporate, centralised model to a more agile, community-driven structure.
modal.s1_rtjl_body: A subsidiary of the Foundation responsible for managing the XRD token treasury. Its primary goal is to secure funding for network development, security, developer incentives and marketing.
modal.s1_role_body: Historically the Foundation acted as a supervisor, delegating code development to external companies. After a major restructuring in 2025 it had to absorb part of the technical team and create an internal development group to maintain key systems such as Radix Wallet and Gateway services.
modal.s1_strategy_body: 2025 was an extremely hard year, marked by sharp market falls and the tragic loss of founder Dan Hughes. The Foundation's strategy for 2026 is to focus on operational efficiency, with the long-term goal of becoming "unnecessary" by transferring power to the community through decentralised RFP processes.
modal.s2_split_body: To avoid conflicts of interest, Dan Hughes and Piers Ridyard announced a split. RDX Works stopped handling the network core and now operates as a commercial application incubator within the ecosystem, such as the Anthic exchange or the Instabridge platform.
modal.s2_cease_body: The Foundation announced it was ending its ongoing development work with RDX Works. When RDX Works abruptly ceased its Radix-related work, the Foundation had to intervene urgently to maintain the infrastructure.
modal.s3_origin_body: This entity was conceived in late 2024 by Dan Hughes himself when he decided to separate operationally from RDX Works. Its goal was to focus exclusively on deep research and development of extreme scalability technologies.
modal.s3_tech_sub: Key projects: Cerberus, Xi'an and Cassandra
modal.s3_tech_body: Radix Labs' vision included the Cerberus consensus algorithm, the Xi'an upgrade, and the experimental Cassandra network — which demonstrated over 2 million TPS in tests. Following Dan's passing, the Foundation is re-evaluating how to continue his technical vision.
modal.s4_radvocates_body: The project has always relied on local leaders who organise events, create hubs and educate new builders on Scrypto, the smart contract programming language of Radix.
modal.s4_defi_body: Much of the DeFi innovation on Radix is being driven independently. Projects like DeXter (an order-book exchange) are built and managed entirely by the community.
modal.s4_transition_body: Radix is in a chapter of historic transition and survival. It has moved from heavy reliance on the private company RDX Works to being under the direct care of the Radix Foundation, which is working hard to stabilise the network and delegate the future of the project to a truly decentralised community.
